title: Jackfruit Nutrient Deficiency: Signs, Causes and the Fertilizer That Fixes It
metaTitle: Jackfruit Nutrient Deficiency: Signs and Fertilizer Fix
metaDescription: Jackfruit nutrient deficiency shows in the leaves. See the signs of nitrogen and potassium in langka, how to be sure, and the fertilizer to apply.
excerpt: Jackfruit nutrient deficiency is one of the first things to check when the leaves of your langka (jackfruit) turn yellow, purple or burnt at the edges. On Philippine farms the usual ones are nitrogen, potassium, phosphorus, boron, zinc, magnesium and iron. This guide shows where each one starts, how to be sure, and the fertilizer that fixes it.

heroImage.alt: Potassium deficiency on a leaf, shown on another crop as a stand in for jackfruit

blocks.text: Start with one question: did the change begin on the old leaves or on the young ones? Nitrogen, potassium, phosphorus and magnesium move inside the plant, so a shortage shows on the old, lower leaves first. But boron, zinc and iron stay where the plant first put them, so the young leaves and the growing tip show it first. After that, the color and the pattern narrow down which jackfruit nutrient deficiency you have, and a soil test confirms it. Each one below has its signs, its causes and its fix.

blocks.caption: Deficiencies that start on the young leaves of langka

Fruits split or crack with a reddish purple color and gum in the cracks. Young leaves yellow and brittle.

blocks.text: Before you buy fertilizer for a jackfruit nutrient deficiency

So use the table to pick the likeliest jackfruit nutrient deficiency, then read its section below. Also keep in mind that dry soil, standing water, cold nights, a pest or a disease can look the same. That is why it pays to check the roots and the whole field first.
Nitrogen deficiency in jackfruit

No jackfruit particular description was found, so this follows general fruit tree signs. The tree first looks light green all over. Then the older, lower leaves turn evenly yellow, veins included, and fall early, while the yellowing slowly moves up to younger leaves. New flushes are short with small leaves, and the tree sets fewer fruits. You see it most at this stage: young trees in the first years after planting, and old bearing trees that never get fertilizer.
Why nitrogen deficiency happens in langka
In the Philippines jackfruit is seldom fertilized, so many trees run short. Sandy or eroded soils low in organic matter, heavy rain that washes nitrogen away.
How to tell it apart

Magnesium deficiency also starts on old leaves, but the yellow sits between the veins while the veins stay green. Jackfruit does not tolerate wet soil, and two or three days of standing water can yellow and kill a tree. To be sure, send a sample of recently matured leaves for a leaf test and a soil sample for a soil test. A clear greening of new leaves within a few weeks after a nitrogen dose confirms it.
What to apply for nitrogen deficiency

For young trees, the Philippine practice described by Coronel gives 100 to 150 grams of Ammonium sulfate 21 0 0 per tree one month after planting and the same again six months later. For fruiting trees it gives 0.5 to 1 kg of Complete 14 14 14 per tree at the start of the rainy season and the same near its end. At least 2 to 3 kg per dose for full grown trees of 15 to 20 years. Spread it in a ring under the canopy edge and water it in.

Sold here with nitrogen: **Atlas Granular Urea** by Atlas Fertilizer Corporation (46 0 0), **YaraVera Viking Ship Granular Urea** by Yara Fertilizers Philippines, Inc. (46 0 0), **Planters Products Granular Urea** by Planters Products, Inc. (46 0 0) and **Harbest Granular Urea** by Harbest Agribusiness Corporation (46 0 0). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [urea fertilizer](/blog/urea-fertilizer), and the page on [nitrogen deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/nitrogen-deficiency) in every crop. In anee.io, Anee, the [smart farm technician](/features/ai-agricultural-technician), reads a photo of the leaf and tells you which nutrient is short.
To keep it away, fertilize every year in two splits, raise the amount as the tree grows.
Potassium deficiency in jackfruit

No jackfruit particular description was found, so this follows general fruit tree signs. The edges and tips of older or newly matured leaves yellow first, then dry brown as a scorch that moves in toward the midrib. Badly hit leaves drop. Fruit and seed production suffers, so fruits are smaller and lower in quality. You see it most at this stage: bearing trees, most of all during fruit growth when the fruit pulls potash from the leaves.
Why potassium deficiency happens in langka
Heavy crops remove potash every year, and most trees get none back. Sandy, leached soils under heavy rain and dry spells that cut uptake make it worse.
How to tell it apart

Magnesium deficiency also hits old leaves but yellows between the veins, not along the edge. Fertilizer burn from too much fertilizer close to the trunk and dry wind can also brown leaf edges. To be sure, A leaf test of recently matured leaves and a soil test for exchangeable potassium.
What to apply for potassium deficiency

Give potash with the yearly fertilizer, following the soil test. In a Samar and Leyte trial on the EVIARC Sweet variety, trees given 0.83 kg Complete 14 14 14, 3.33 kg Solophos and 0.73 kg Muriate of potash 0 0 60 per tree gave bigger pulp and more flakes per fruit than unfertilized trees. TNAU's schedule rises from 0.1 kg potash per tree in the first year to 0.5 kg from the sixth year, in two splits.

Sold here with potassium: **Atlas Muriate of Potash** by Atlas Fertilizer Corporation (0 0 60), **Philphos Muriate of Potash** by Philippine Phosphate Fertilizer Corporation (0 0 60), **Harbest Granular Muriate of Potash** by Harbest Agribusiness Corporation (0 0 60) and **Swire Muriate of Potash** by Swire Agrotech Agricultural Products Inc. (0 0 60). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [potash fertilizer](/blog/potash-fertilizer), and the page on [potassium deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/potassium-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, include potash every year, split in two doses, and return leaves and fruit waste to the ring as compost.
Phosphorus deficiency in jackfruit

No jackfruit particular description was found, so this follows general fruit tree signs. Growth is slow and the tree stays small. Older leaves lose their shine and take on a purple or bronze color, most of all on the underside. Roots stay weak and young trees take longer to start bearing. You see it most at this stage: young trees after planting, and trees on very acid soils.
Why phosphorus deficiency happens in langka
Acid soils that lock phosphorus up, soils low in organic matter, and cold or waterlogged soil.
How to tell it apart

Cool weather, drought and root damage can also slow growth and redden leaves, so check the soil moisture and the roots. Nitrogen deficiency makes old leaves pale yellow rather than purple or bronze. To be sure, A soil test for available phosphorus and pH, and a leaf test.
What to apply for phosphorus deficiency

Apply a phosphorus fertilizer in a ring under the canopy and work it into the topsoil, following the soil test. The Samar and Leyte trial used 3.33 kg Solophos (Superphosphate 0 20 0) per tree with complete fertilizer and potash. TNAU's schedule gives 0.08 kg phosphorus per tree in the first year, rising to 0.4 kg from the sixth year. Lime very acid soils so the phosphorus stays available.

Sold here with phosphorus: **Triple Super Phosphate** by Newman Chemicals Corporation (0 46 0), **Sagrex Duofos Granular Guano Phosphate** by Sagrex Corporation (0 22 0 (guano phosphate)), **Philphos 18 46 0** by Philippine Phosphate Fertilizer Corporation (18 46 0 (diammonium phosphate)) and **Atlas Di Ammonium Phosphate** by Atlas Fertilizer Corporation (18 46 0). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [16 20 0 fertilizer](/blog/16-20-0-fertilizer), and the page on [phosphorus deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/phosphorus-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, mix compost and a phosphorus fertilizer into the planting soil, and add some every year.
Boron deficiency in jackfruit

Fruits split or crack, and the cracks show a reddish purple color with gum oozing out. Young leaves turn yellow, thin and brittle, and the shoot tips grow poorly. Flowers can drop before they are pollinated, which leaves misshapen fruit. You see it most at this stage: flowering and fruit growth, and on new flushes.
Why boron deficiency happens in langka
Sandy or leached soils low in organic matter, dry spells, and heavy liming. Boron moves little inside the tree, so young tissue and fruit show it first.
How to tell it apart

Rhizopus fruit rot makes young fruits go soft and grey black with mould, not dry cracks with gum. Fruit borers leave holes with frass. To be sure, do a soil test, as Kerala Agricultural University advises, and a leaf test for boron. Cracked fruit together with yellow, brittle young leaves points to boron.
What to apply for boron deficiency

Kerala Agricultural University gives Borax at 4 kg per acre (about 10 kg per hectare) to the soil, or a foliar spray of Borax at 1 gram per liter. Do not mix boron with calcium fertilizers or apply it together with ammonium fertilizers. Too much boron is toxic, so do not repeat high doses without a test.

Sold here with boron: **Solubor** by Caldic Philippines Inc. (21 percent boron), **Etifert 11 (Borax Decahydrate)** by Zetryl.Chem Phils., Inc. (11 percent boron), **YaraVita BORTRAC 150** by Yara Fertilizers Philippines, Inc. (11.1 percent boron) and **Grow More Liquid Chelate Boron** by Sagrex Corporation (10 percent boron). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [foliar fertilizer](/blog/foliar-fertilizer), and the page on [boron deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/boron-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, keep organic matter up, water during long dry spells, and add a small boron dose on soils that tested low.
Zinc deficiency in jackfruit

New leaves come out small with short stalks and crowd together at the shoot tip in a rosette. They yellow between the veins and can show yellow streaks. Fruits stay smaller and more of them drop, so the yield falls. You see it most at this stage: new flushes, flowering and early fruit growth.
Why zinc deficiency happens in langka
Zinc is the most common micronutrient shortage of fruit crops. Soils with pH outside about 5 to 7.5, heavy phosphate fertilizer, and sandy or eroded soils bring it on.
How to tell it apart

Iron deficiency also yellows young leaves between the veins, but the leaves stay normal in size and do not rosette. Mites and thrips can also stunt new leaves. To be sure, A soil test for zinc and pH, and a leaf test. New leaves that come out normal after a zinc spray on a few branches confirm it.
What to apply for zinc deficiency

TNAU gives a foliar spray of 500 grams Zinc sulfate, 250 grams lime and 100 grams urea with 100 ml soap in 100 liters of water (5 grams Zinc sulfate per liter), three times at 20 day intervals, plus 250 grams Zinc sulfate per tree mixed with compost or manure in two equal doses when the tree puts out new growth. Kerala Agricultural University gives 8 kg Zinc sulfate per acre (about 20 kg per hectare) on deficient soils. Do not apply zinc and phosphate fertilizer at the same time.

Sold here with zinc: **Harvester Zinc Sulphate Heptahydrate** by Universal Harvester, Inc. (22 percent zinc), **Great Planters Zinc Sulphate Heptahydrate** by Agway Chemicals Corp. (21 percent zinc), **Zinc Sulphate Monohydrate** by Petbowe Trading Corporation (33 percent zinc) and **YaraVita ZINTRAC 700** by Yara Fertilizers Philippines, Inc. (40 percent zinc). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [fertilizer with zinc](/blog/micronutrients-for-rice), and the page on [zinc deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/zinc-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, avoid heavy phosphate, keep organic matter up, and include zinc in the program on soils that tested low.
Magnesium deficiency in jackfruit

Older, lower leaves turn yellow between the side veins on both sides of the midrib while the veins stay green. The yellow starts at the leaf edge and moves in toward the midrib. Later the yellow parts turn reddish with dead patches, and the leaves drop early. You see it most at this stage: bearing trees, often after heavy potash fertilizer.
Why magnesium deficiency happens in langka
Acid, sandy and leached soils, and heavy potash fertilizer, which competes with magnesium.
How to tell it apart

Potassium deficiency also hits old leaves, but it burns the leaf edge brown instead of yellowing between the veins. Nitrogen deficiency yellows the whole old leaf, veins included. To be sure, do a soil test for magnesium, potassium and calcium, as Kerala Agricultural University advises, and a leaf test.
What to apply for magnesium deficiency

Kerala Agricultural University gives 32 kg Magnesium sulfate per acre (about 80 kg per hectare) in bands near the trees. TNAU gives 1.5 kg Dolomite per tree per year to the soil and a foliar spray of Magnesium sulfate at 30 to 50 grams per liter. That is a strong mix, so test it on a few branches first. Do not apply magnesium and potassium fertilizers together.

Sold here with magnesium: **Dolomite** by A6 Agrisource Limited Corporation (24 percent calcium and 11 percent magnesium), **YaraTera KRISTA MgS** by Yara Fertilizers Philippines, Inc. (16 percent MgO and 13 percent sulfur), **Magnepro** by Ramgo International Corporation (16 percent MgO and 12.8 percent sulfur) and **Lucky Planters Magnesium Sulphate Heptahydrate (Epsom Salt)** by Mindanao Agriplus Corporation (16.27 percent MgO and 13 percent sulfur). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [complete fertilizer](/blog/complete-fertilizer-14-14-14), and the page on [magnesium deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/magnesium-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, use Dolomite when liming acid soils, and keep potash and magnesium in balance based on a soil test.
Iron deficiency in jackfruit

Young leaves yellow between the veins while the veins and midrib stay green. In bad cases the whole young leaf turns yellow, though the midrib can stay green, and growth is stunted. Older leaves usually stay green. You see it most at this stage: new flushes, mostly on high pH soils or after waterlogging.
Why iron deficiency happens in langka
Iron is plentiful in most acid Philippine soils, so true shortage is uncommon. It shows on limestone, coralline or overlimed soils with high pH, and in waterlogged soil.
How to tell it apart

Zinc deficiency also yellows young leaves between the veins, but the leaves are small and bunched. Manganese deficiency shows on fully grown leaves as a mix of green and yellow between the main veins. To be sure, A soil test for pH and iron. Kerala soils are often high in iron.
What to apply for iron deficiency

On deficient soils Kerala Agricultural University gives Ferrous sulfate at 6 kg per acre (about 15 kg per hectare). UF IFAS advises chelated iron (EDDHA) as a soil drench on high pH soils, since iron sprays on the leaves generally work poorly. Ferrous sulfate to the soil on acid soils. Improve drainage where water stands.

Sold here with iron: **Ferrous Sulphate Heptahydrate** by Cleveland Industries Inc. (20 percent iron), **Ferrous Sulfate Monohydrate** by Zetryl.Chem Phils., Inc. (30 percent iron), **Grow More Liquid Chelate Iron with Sulfur** by Sagrex Corporation (5 percent iron and 3 percent sulfur) and **Biozome** by Manchem Industries, Inc. (12 percent S, 12 percent Zn, 3 percent Mn, 1 percent Mg, 1 percent Fe, 1 percent Cu, 0.5 percent B, 0.05 percent Mo). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [foliar fertilizer](/blog/foliar-fertilizer), and the page on [iron deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/iron-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, do not overlime, drain wet spots, and keep potash up.

blocks.title: Let a soil test decide the rate
blocks.text: A soil test is the surest check for any jackfruit nutrient deficiency. Before you buy, ask your Municipal Agriculture Office where to send a soil sample. The DA regional soil laboratories and the Bureau of Soils and Water Management test soil, and the result says how much of each fertilizer your langka needs. That saves money, because extra fertilizer is money lost.

blocks.text: Jackfruit nutrient deficiency questions

items.q: Why are my langka leaves turning yellow?
items.a: The most common cause is nitrogen deficiency: the whole canopy turns pale green, older leaves go yellow and drop, and new shoots stay short. If the young leaves turn yellow first instead, look at boron deficiency.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes nitrogen deficiency in jackfruit?
items.a: For young trees, the Philippine practice described by Coronel gives 100 to 150 grams of Ammonium sulfate 21 0 0 per tree one month after planting and the same again six months later. For fruiting trees it gives 0.5 to 1 kg of Complete 14 14 14 per tree at the start of the rainy season and the same near its end.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes potassium deficiency in jackfruit?
items.a: Give potash with the yearly fertilizer, following the soil test. In a Samar and Leyte trial on the EVIARC Sweet variety, trees given 0.83 kg Complete 14 14 14, 3.33 kg Solophos and 0.73 kg Muriate of potash 0 0 60 per tree gave bigger pulp and more flakes per fruit than unfertilized trees.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes phosphorus deficiency in jackfruit?
items.a: Apply a phosphorus fertilizer in a ring under the canopy and work it into the topsoil, following the soil test. The Samar and Leyte trial used 3.33 kg Solophos (Superphosphate 0 20 0) per tree with complete fertilizer and potash.

items.q: How do I know which nutrient my langka lacks?
items.a: First look at where the change began, on the old leaves or the young ones, then at the color and the pattern. Next, confirm the jackfruit nutrient deficiency with a soil test or a leaf test before you buy fertilizer.
